beats.headline: Not yet, says Mordecai
beats.text: Mordecai, freshly woken and slurring slightly, runs through the ranks of boss for two new crawlers: Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, and Floor. There are also others, he adds, but those are called elites. You won't need to worry about them just yet. Then Carl asks about what they just fought: the most common type of boss, Mordecai confirms, and now they know how to recognise its lair.

beats.headline: Meet an Elite
beats.text: The first one on the record is Tsarina Signet, half naiad, half high elf, a level-sixty summoner whose tattoos move. Her description says it outright: This is an Elite. An achievement follows. Elites are powerful, one-of-a-kind entities, the non-boss, non-divine hero class; they either want to fuck you or kill you, and always want to use you. Where there is one, there are usually more. Reward: elites now show on the map as dots with a black cross. Mordecai says to get out.

beats.headline: Printed for somebody else's show
beats.text: Mordecai explains, having already said to stay away. Thousands of elites are spread through the urban floors, and they travel between them. They are never naturals: designed, printed, imprinted with the memories their drama needs, so as far as they know this is the real world. Every storyline has its own writers, who hot patch new instructions into an elite's mind when the plot drifts. Most have thick plot armour. In their stories, a crawler is the extra, the red shirt, the guest star.

beats.headline: An elite and a city boss
beats.text: Ringmaster Grimaldi, a Pestiferous Vine as tall as the tent, is labelled This is an Elite and Level 85 City Boss in the same breath. Carl, in the bleachers with his poison ready, messages Mordecai: nobody said they could be both. On the way in he passed Apollon the Mighty, a strongman ogre selling petrified ice cream, also an elite, his dot red with a cross. Mordecai has warned him more than once that when it comes to elites, the rules don't mean shit.

beats.headline: A contract to play along
beats.text: With the vine poisoned, Carl sends Zev a message for the producers of Vengeance of the Daughter. He wants to be on their show, as a regular. If he and Donut survive the night and reach the sixth floor, he signs an exclusive agreement to complete only the elite-themed quests there that belong to their storyline. The alternative, he explains, is that he un-poisons Grimaldi with his own blood and their big night is a dud. Zev's boss patches them in.

beats.headline: A gnoll on the dance floor
beats.text: In the members-only room of the Desperado Club, three elites work the floor, white dots with crosses, each in conversation with a crawler, and an elephant-headed one leads three humans into the back. Quint the opossum explains the closed playroom: a crawler with one goat leg and two dogs froze the whole room with a spell, stole tequila, and splattered the brains of an elite gnoll who had been talking to her. Carl knows the description. Lucia Mar.

beats.headline: A coveted ninth-floor slot
beats.text: At the negotiating table, Quasar slips in an old emergency-use rule, and the kua-tin agree to keep it quiet. It guarantees Vengeance of the Daughter the equivalent of a third season. What makes that valuable is where it leads: not all secondary programs are allowed to send their elites to the ninth floor. It is a coveted reward, Quasar insists the producers are sure to leap at it, and it gives them one more reason to keep Carl alive.

beats.headline: Suggestions, not strings
beats.text: Two of Signet's were-castors insist on walking Carl and Donut back to a saferoom, and it takes Carl a minute to see why: Signet pushed them, and the showrunners pushed Signet, because Odette's show is in a few hours. Elites are not nearly as autonomous as regular NPCs. They are not controlled like robots, but showrunners may send them suggestions that make them act out of character. Carl wonders whether an elite could be made self-aware, like other NPCs, and what would happen then.

beats.headline: What the hunters leave alone
beats.text: A note in the cookbook from Drakea, 22nd edition, on the sixth floor's hunters: they avoid the elites. They are smart enough not to fight something they are not allowed to defeat easily. The trouble for crawlers is that elites are more dangerous than the hunters and much more numerous, and they should always be avoided. Some of the more powerful hunters hunt elites anyway, for the equipment and the clout. The note calls it a most dangerous game.

beats.headline: A storyline off the leash
beats.text: Miriam Dom's calls for help reach Carl late, carried by other crawlers, and the keyword in the previews explains the delay: Elite. Carl cannot help where an elite is involved. Miriam answers that the elite is dead and the quest is done; Pony killed him and was paralysed doing it. The rest follows. A vampire sickness is spreading through the dinosaurs of the forest, part of the elite's story, and he died before it could be stopped. For once, not something Carl or Donut started.

beats.headline: The main show does not share
beats.text: Carl lays it out for the other crawlers before the high elves' party. Queen Imogen is a country boss, and they are probably going to have to fight her at the end of the party. His elite quest wants to fight the same boss before or during it, which means it is doomed: the main showrunners are not going to let a secondary production hose their climax. He likes Signet. He would like to avoid going down with her. He has already told her to her face: attack when the party starts and she is dead.

beats.headline: Stay away from any elites
beats.text: A message from Quasar waits on arrival. The contract for Vengeance of the Daughter, with the third season they negotiated, is about to haunt them: Sensation Entertainment has been bought by a subsidiary of the Dream, and the new owners are demanding their season. Signet is not coming back, so whatever happens is going to be something stupid, and the new showrunners are going to try to use Carl's obligation against him. For now: stay the fuck away from any elites you see.

beats.headline: Herman the Fleet
beats.text: In the Princess Posse's castle, the only other dot on the map is an elite: Herman the Fleet, ogre strongman, a legionnaire of the Princess Posse, third brother of Grimaldi's strongmen. He is writhing at a desk. He has been waiting. Supposed to do it already. Been fighting it. Tell brother sorry. He is wearing explosive satchels. The orc adjutant steps out and kills him with an axe, then calls foul: an unlawful assassination attempt by Sensation Entertainment, exerting undue influence on one of their elites.
